item.title: FIA announces ADUO results following third review periods of 2026
item.description:
Sport news

Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) is a mechanism within the 2026 Formula 1 Technical Regulations (Article C4) allowing Power Unit manufacturers whose Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) performance falls at least 2% below the best-performing ICE across defined review periods to introduce additional homologated upgrades to their Power Unit during the current and following season, but also to benefit from additional Cost Cap and dyno testing allowances. The level of ADUO is calculated over three periods in each season, with the level of allowance determined by the size of the performance gap to the leading ICE. The first review period was concluded after the Canadian Grand Prix, the second review period concluded after the Hungarian Grand Prix and the third review period concluded after the United States Grand Prix. 

The FIA can confirm that the results of the third ADUO analysis period of 2026 (Races 12 to 18) have been communicated to all Power Unit manufacturers. 

For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers. 

Due to the confidential nature of this information, no further details on Power Unit performance index measurements will be communicated. 

As a reminder, the following results were communicated for period 1 of 2026: 

  • Mercedes were determined to be in the 2-4% window, and are thus allowed 1 additional homologation in 2026 and an additional 1 in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases. 

  • Audi, Ferrari and Honda were determined to be above 4%, and are thus allowed 2 additional homologations in 2026 and 2 in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases. 

For period 2, no additional homologations were granted to any Power Unit Manufacturers. 

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Director of Single Seater, said: “The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached."

The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the Power Unit Manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons." 

The next ADUO review period will start in 2027 and will cover races 1 to 6 (Bahrain to Miami). 

ENDS 

Note to editors: More information about ADUO can be found here. 

The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility. 

Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.

item.title: Al-Attiyah and Delfino secure clean sweep of FIA Middle East Baja Cup successes with Qatari’s fourth win in the Dubai International Baja
item.description:
Sport news

Nasser Saleh Al-Attiyah teamed up with Frenchman Max Delfino to secure a fourth victory in the Dubai International Baja and wrap up a clean sweep of four victories on rounds of the 2026 FIA Middle East Baja Cup.

The Qatari guided his Optimus MD Rallye to back-to-back stage wins on a demanding route through the Al-Qudra desert in the United Arab Emirates to add another Baja success to the 10 Dubai International Rally wins he earned before the event switched to a Baja-style format in 2016.

Based at Dubai Festival City and organised by the Emirates Motorsports Organisation (EMSO), thirty-one of the original 35 crews made the final start list for the 10th edition with seven registered in the Ultimate category, eight in Challenger, a dozen in SSV and four in the Stock class.

The South Racing Can-Am Team’s Mitchel van den Brink came into the weekend needing a strong finish to snatch the FIA World Baja Cup title from Francisco Barreto’s clutches. The Dutchman started strongly with a good result on the Prologue and then finished second behind Al-Attiyah on the opening stage.

He shadowed the Qatari to the finish of the last timed section to secure second place, albeit 5min 18.7sec behind the winner, to win the world title in a Can-Am Maverick Challenger and also confirm success in the Challenger category.

Van den Brink said: “It was a very nice last stage and we pushed from the beginning. We had a nice flow and a nice rhythm. We knew at the refuelling zone that we were one minute ahead of Nasser. We knew we had created a big gap to the others and we took it safe. We were just two seconds behind Nasser (stage two). It doesn’t matter. First in the World Cup. We became world champions in the Challenger and the overall.”

Francisco Barreto and Paulo Fiúza were penalised for an offence on the Prologue, recovered to finish fourth in the opening stage but retired early on the final day with engine problems and lost their chance of claiming the world titles. Van den Brink’s navigator Bart van Heun duly became the champion navigator for the 2026 season. He had already won the Challenger Navigators’ title.

A disappointed Barreto, who finished second in the FIA World Baja Cup, said: “We had engine problems at kilometre 50, no oil pressure in the engine. The points that the organisation took from us on the Prologue, maybe we could win the World Cup. It’s what it is…”

Sergei Remennik and Aleksei Ignatov were not registered for either Baja series but rounded off the podium places in a Taurus T3 Max.

Oman’s Hamed Al-Wahaibi may have missed out on the Challenger title to van den Brink but the Omani finished his season strongly with fourth place alongside François Cazalet. That result catapulted the veteran into third in the overall Drivers’ Championship.

Al-Wahaibi said: “The season went very well. We had issues every rally, whether it’s over-speeding, crashing or mechanical and that didn’t help the overall situation. We didn’t have a chance in Challenger. Mitch (Van den Brink) was flying. He won the T3 and the overall.”

The local crew of Mansour Al-Helai and Khalid Al-Kendi finished fifth in a Can-Am Maverick R and collected enough points to secure the FIA World Baja Cup’s SSV titles. Norwegian Hedda Hosås suffered brake issues on the first selective section and had to settle for second in the championship with her navigator Pol Tibau. They finished 11th overall and earned the fastest SSV time on the second stage.

“For me, since I am a child, I always dream of being a world champion and today I am,” said Al-Helei. “The stage was full of drama. My engine was overheating for exactly 180km. So, I was driving very slow, but I wanted to bring it to the finish. I feel very excited, very honoured.”

R-X Sport’s Rashid Al-Ketbi and Oriol Mena came home in 14th and third of the SSV crews in the FIA World Baja Cup. But a time penalty for missing way points dropped the Emirati to 18th overall.

Majed Al-Thunayyan and Omar Al-Lahim got the better of Abdulla Al-Rabban and Ali Al-Ajami to seize victory in the Stock category to add to their championship title. It was the Saudi’s third success in Dubai in four years. Al-Rabban had broken both wishbones, a link rod and the crown gear on his Nissan Patrol on the first stage.

Al-Mashna and Abdullah Al-Shammeri failed to finish the season’s finale but were classified second in the championship standings.

In a late update to the itinerary, the Emirates Motorsports Organisation (EMSO) hosted the short 4.80km Prologue at Mushrif Park for the first time.

Barreto repeated his Qatar success from the previous weekend and clocked the fastest time of 2min 55.9sec to win the short test by 5.6 seconds from title rival Saood Variawa. Aliyyah Koloc came home in third with Challenger and SSV bragging rights going to fourth-placed Sergei Remennik and Rashid Al-Ketbi in seventh.

Martin Koloc retired after incurring a 10-minute penalty for losing a wheel on the stage and there were surprise 12-minute penalties for both Al-Shammeri and Al-Attiyah for not starting the Prologue. Hamed Al-Harbi also incurred a 10-minute penalty for a missing wheel in the Prologue.

Barreto was later disqualified from the results of the Prologue. It came to light from video evidence that the Portuguese had not used notes provided by Baja officials for the short opening stage. As a result, the Prologue win went to Variawa with Barreto pushed down to start the opening desert stage from 29th position. More importantly, he lost his Prologue points.

The rolling dunes of the Al-Qudra desert hosted the opening selective section of 178.02km on Saturday morning. Al-Attiyah led the way from Variawa, Al-Ketbi and Van den Brink.

The Qatari stopped the clocks in 2hr 41min 59.9sec and moved into a 5min 16sec lead over Challenger pace-setter Van den Brink. Al-Helai led the SSVs in third and Barreto battled his way through the tail-enders to claim the fourth quickest time.

Van den Brink said: “Second overall, first in the World Cup and only five minutes behind Nasser is not bad with the Challenger. We were in a good flow. He (Nasser) set up some nice lines and we were following them.”

Technical issues ruined Variawa’s challenge for FIA World Baja Cup glory and he was sidelined. Likewise, a collision with another competing vehicle and damage sustained to his South Racing Can-Am forced Argentina’s Fernando Alvarez out of the three-way fight for SSV title honours. Khalid Al-Jafla and Andrei Rudnitskiy also retired their Toyota Hilux Evo after an accident.

Alvarez said: “Another driver hit us very hard from the side and we rolled several times. Neither of us were injured but it ended our possibility of winning the World Championship that we led until this event.”

The second Al-Faqa’a selective section ran for 179.56km. Al-Attiyah claimed the stage win and did enough to earn a fourth Dubai Baja victory, with Van den Brink prevailing in the FIA World Baja Cup.  

El-Shamy shadows Al-Attiyah through the FIA Middle Baja Cup finale

Al-Attiyah may have dominated this year’s FIA Middle East Baja Cup with Max Delfino but it was also a successful finale to the season for Ahmed El-Shamy and his navigator Leonard Cremer.

The Century CR6 driver confirmed the runner-up spot in the regional Ultimate category in Qatar recently. A sixth-place finish in Dubai and points for second in the Middle East Baja Cup were sufficient for the Egyptian to seal third in the overall Drivers’ Championship and Master Driver honours. Rival Yasir Seaidan had graced the original entry list but was a non-starter.

The UAE-based British pairing of David Mabbs and Dave McBride reached the finish in 10th overall and third in the regional Baja points. With Seaidan failing to start, they were able to confirm the regional Challenger titles in a Can-Am Maverick X3.

Qatari Mohammed Al-Marri confirmed success in the regional SSV title race by finishing 12th overall with French navigator Pierre Delorme and also second in the main Drivers’ Championship. Fellow countryman Mohammed Al-Atteya claimed the runner-up spot with his co-pilot Aleksei Kuzmich topping the SSV Navigators’ Championship standings in the regional Baja series in 13th.

The Qatari finished just ahead of the Saudi pairing of Hamad Al-Harbi and Faisal Al-Suwayh and Ahmed Al-Kuwari with his navigator Augusto Sanz. Al-Kuwari was driving a new Can Am Maverick R in the Experimental category and was not classified in the final results. He had already secured the Teams’ Championship through his Al-Kuwari Racing by Apex operation.

Camelia Liparoti (Yamaha) incurred half an hour of time penalties on the opening stage for missing waypoints but reached the finish in 15th with navigator Erika Mingozzi.

Saudi Abdullah Al-Shegawi and his Emirati navigator Ali Mirza retired on the second stage but still secured both regional Stock titles in their Toyota Prado.

The Baja was held under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al-Maktoum. Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai.

It was supported by the Dubai Government and its key entities, including Dubai Police, the Roads and Transport Authority, the Dubai Municipality and official automotive partner, Al-Futtaim Toyota.

item.title: F1 – Norris triumphs in São Paulo as Mercedes secure 2026 Constructors’ Championship
item.description:
Sport news

Lando Norris converted pole position into victory at the 2026 FIA Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix, mastering changing conditions at Interlagos to take the chequered flag 14.6 seconds clear of Max Verstappen. The Red Bull driver produced a remarkable recovery from 21st on the grid to finish second, with team-mate Isack Hadjar completing the podium in third, while Mercedes secured the Constructors’ Championship with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli finishing fourth and fifth respectively.

Norris claimed his third victory of the season after negotiating a demanding 71-lap contest that began on Intermediate tyres before switching to slicks and eventually returning to intermediates as rain arrived in the closing stages. The McLaren driver maintained his composure throughout, responding to challenges from Mercedes and Red Bull to take the win in a race punctuated by spins, strategy changes and shifting track conditions.

At the start, Antonelli made the most of his second-place grid position to take the lead into Turn 1, while Norris lost ground from pole position. Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson also made an excellent getaway, moving around the outside of the McLaren into the opening corner before taking second place through Turn 2.

Further back, Lewis Hamilton made an impressive start to his 400th Formula 1 appearance, climbing from 20th on the grid to ninth by the end of the opening lap. Verstappen was also immediately on the move, advancing from 21st to 13th as the field negotiated the opening sequence of corners.

The four-time World Champion continued his charge, reaching eighth by Lap 5 after passing Oscar Piastri and Alexander Albon in quick succession. Hamilton, meanwhile, was investigated for passing Oliver Bearman off the track on the opening lap and subsequently handed the position back to the Haas driver, dropping to 11th.

As the Intermediate tyres began to overheat on the drying circuit, Lawson's early advantage disappeared. Norris, Hadjar and Russell all passed the Racing Bulls driver, with Verstappen also making progress after moving ahead of Nico Hülkenberg.

Hamilton was among the first to switch to slicks, pitting at the end of Lap 14 for soft tyres. Albon followed one lap later, triggering a wave of pit stops as teams responded to the rapidly improving track conditions.

Norris, Russell and Hadjar came in at the end of Lap 16, while Antonelli and Verstappen stayed out for another lap. However, Russell's stop was followed by a costly spin at the pit-lane exit. The Mercedes driver lost time as he attempted to recover, briefly making contact with the wall before rejoining the circuit.

Antonelli and Verstappen eventually pitted at the end of Lap 17. The Mercedes driver retained the lead, but Norris had reduced the deficit to approximately two seconds. Verstappen rejoined fourth, behind Hadjar, who had moved into third.

Norris immediately began closing on Antonelli, taking almost a second out of the gap on the following lap. The Mercedes driver reported an issue with the car before spinning at Turn 1 on Lap 20, allowing Norris to take the lead. Antonelli rejoined just ahead of Hadjar but ran wide at the same corner one lap later, allowing the Red Bull driver through into second.

Verstappen was also closing in, and Antonelli's difficult sequence continued when he ran deep at Turn 1 again, dropping behind his compatriot. By Lap 23, the track was declared completely dry and Overtake Mode was enabled, with Norris holding a 3.3-second advantage over Hadjar and Verstappen approximately seven seconds behind.

With the threat of further rain being reported, Norris gradually extended his advantage. Hadjar remained second, with Verstappen third, while Antonelli slipped further back after his earlier spins. Further down the order, Albon and Fernando Alonso fought over 11th place, with the Williams driver receiving a five-second penalty following an incident at Turn 1 on Lap 35.

At the front, Verstappen began closing on Hadjar. The Dutchman moved ahead of his team-mate into Turn 1 on Lap 38, with Norris now enjoying a lead of more than nine seconds. Hadjar remained close enough to challenge, while the expected rain shower initially appeared to be missing the circuit.

Hamilton, having stopped for another set of soft tyres, began setting competitive lap times and eventually unlapped himself from Norris on Lap 44. Verstappen, meanwhile, made his second stop at the end of Lap 45, rejoining fifth behind Piastri and Russell. Red Bull opted to keep Hadjar on track, with the Frenchman reporting only light drops of rain.

Norris made his second stop at the end of Lap 49, returning in fourth place. He quickly passed Piastri, while Red Bull brought Hadjar in one lap later. The rookie rejoined sixth but moved up to fifth when Piastri made his own stop on Lap 51.

Antonelli subsequently surrendered the lead to pit at the end of Lap 53, rejoining behind Russell and Hadjar. The Red Bull driver moved ahead of the Mercedes into Turn 4, putting himself back into podium contention as the rain began to intensify.

Russell was instructed to allow Antonelli through at the start of Lap 57, while Lawson moved ahead of Charles Leclerc for seventh. Norris continued to lead by approximately 10 seconds, with Verstappen second and Hadjar third, although Antonelli was closing on the Red Bull as the deteriorating conditions made the circuit increasingly difficult to navigate.

The rain eventually became heavy enough to prompt a return to intermediate tyres. Russell and Alonso were the first to pit at the end of Lap 61, with the remainder of the field following as grip levels dropped rapidly.

Hamilton's recovery suffered a setback when he spun on the climb towards the final sector, brushing the wall before managing to return to the pits. Antonelli also came under investigation after emerging from his pit box into the path of an Alpine.

With Russell now on fresher intermediates, Mercedes instructed Antonelli to surrender fourth place to his team-mate, which the Italian duly did. The order remained unchanged at the front as Norris completed the final laps to secure victory in 1:35:23.504.

Verstappen crossed the line 14.602 seconds later to take second, completing an outstanding recovery from the back of the grid. Hadjar made it a double podium for Red Bull, finishing 24.485 seconds behind Norris to secure his second podium of the season.

Russell and Antonelli followed in fourth and fifth, respectively, with their results confirming Mercedes as the 2026 Constructors' Champions. Piastri finished sixth for McLaren, ahead of Leclerc, who overtook Lawson on the penultimate lap after a close battle between the pair.

Lawson secured eighth for Racing Bulls, while Hamilton finished ninth after an eventful afternoon that saw him climb from 20th on the grid. Hülkenberg completed the top 10 for Audi.

Mercedes, meanwhile, had the ultimate cause for celebration, securing the 2026 Constructors' Championship with two races still to come.
